query_text: Make a mobile app that handles removing an OAuth token revocation confirmation so I can just disconnect a connected account in one tap without being asked the same thing twice, because going through multiple confirmation steps every time is such a waste. The app should list all linked connections on one screen, let me tap to remove one, and just do it cleanly with a simple final check before the token gets killed.

Create a mobile app for managing posts where I can detach photos or videos from a post while keeping all the text I already wrote completely intact, because sometimes I upload the wrong image and I just want to swap it out without losing my caption. The post editor screen should clearly show the attached media and let me remove it with one tap, leaving my written content right where it was.

Create a mobile app for managing scheduled posts where I can cancel a post that is set to go out later and have it saved back as a draft automatically, so I do not have to rewrite anything if I change my mind. On the scheduled posts screen I want to be able to tap a post, hit cancel, and have it move right into my drafts folder with everything still there.

Make a mobile app for handling incoming friend requests where I can decline a request and also choose to block that person at the same time in one smooth step, because having to do it separately is annoying when someone keeps sending requests. When I tap on a pending request on my phone it should give me the option to just decline, or to decline and block, so I can deal with it once and move on.

Need a mobile app that lets me pause a subscription and shows me a clear window of time where I can still ask for a refund before the pause locks in, because sometimes I forget to cancel in time and I need to know exactly how long I have. The app should show my active subscriptions, let me tap to pause one, and display a plain countdown of the refund grace period so I know where I stand.

A mobile data cleanup tool where I can pick which categories of saved data to wipe from the app, like only clearing my search history or only my saved addresses, instead of having to reset everything at once. The main screen for my phone should show a simple list of data categories I can check off, then confirm and clear just those selected ones, so I stop losing settings I actually want to keep.

Need a mobile app for managing shared documents where I can find a co-author and take away their ability to edit a specific document, switching them down to read-only, because sometimes a project is done and I just want to lock it down. The document manager should list everyone who has write access to each file so I can tap on a name and change their permission right from my phone.

Need a mobile app for managing alert rules where I can switch off a rule so it stops firing but the rule itself stays saved in an archive so I can turn it back on later if I need it, because deleting rules and recreating them from scratch is a huge hassle. On my phone the alert manager should have a clear active versus archived list and let me move a rule between the two with a single tap.

Build a mobile app for managing referral codes where I can set an expiry date on individual codes and also select multiple codes at once to deactivate them all in one go, because manually turning off codes one by one when a campaign ends takes way too long. The app for my phone should show all my active codes in a list, let me pick several at once, and kill them with a single confirm tap.

Build a mobile app for managing linked payment methods where I can remove a connected bank account and have the app show me the current balance and any pending charges before I confirm, so I know there is nothing left to process before I cut the connection. On my phone the account manager should pull up the balance summary clearly and then let me confirm the unlink in one final step.

Build a profile editor app where the pronouns and identity section feels thoughtful and personal, not like a government form, so people can pick from a few gentle preset options or just type in whatever feels right for them. The vibe on mobile should be soft and welcoming, with enough breathing room that filling in your identity feels like self-expression, and the free-text field should sit right alongside the presets so nothing feels hidden or secondary.

Create a mobile setup guide app that walks someone through filling in their emergency contacts and basic health details one calm step at a time, like a gentle checklist that actually feels reassuring rather than clinical. The flow on your phone should have a warm, caring aesthetic with clear sections for each type of information, so by the end you feel prepared rather than overwhelmed.

Need a mobile app for volunteer profiles that lets someone describe the causes they care about and the skills they can offer in a way that feels genuine and human, not like a resume. The profile on your phone should have a warm, community-driven look where you can write a little about why certain causes matter to you and list a handful of skills in a way that feels personal rather than just a checkbox list.

Create a mobile profile app for legal professionals where they can fill in their bar registration details in a way that still feels polished and dignified, because credentials deserve to be presented well. The app on your phone should give each piece of information room to breathe, with a clean, authoritative feel, so your bar number and practice area come across as credentials worth trusting rather than just data in a form.

A patient health baseline app for mobile where someone setting up telemedicine access can fill in their ongoing conditions, past procedures, and regular medications in a calm and organized way, almost like a quiet personal health journal. The profile on your phone should feel reassuring rather than sterile, with clearly separated sections for different parts of your health history so a doctor reading it can get a real picture of you as a person.

Make a mobile profile app for a religious community where members can fill in their role in the congregation and any groups they belong to, with a look and feel that is warm and reverent rather than generic. On your phone the profile should feel like it belongs to a real spiritual community, with a gentle color palette and clear sections for things like your role, your ministry involvements, and a short personal note.

Need a mobile app where I can set up a personal finance profile that captures how I actually think about money, like whether I am saving for something specific, how cautious or relaxed I am with spending, and what my rough monthly budget is, so the app can tailor things to my style. The profile setup on my phone should feel like a thoughtful quiz with a calm, organized aesthetic rather than a bunch of intimidating numbers.

A profile builder for an expat community app on mobile where members can set their home city, the languages they speak, and where they are currently living, all presented in a way that feels warm and global rather than like filling out a visa application. The profile screen on your phone should feel inviting, like a little window into where someone is from and where they are now, with a light and friendly design that makes people actually want to fill it in.

Create a buyer profile app for an online marketplace where people can see and build up their trust score over time, with a look that feels credible and clean rather than cluttered, because first impressions matter when you are buying from strangers. The profile on your phone should display the trust score prominently in a way that feels earned and honest, with a calm visual style that makes buyers look reliable to sellers.

Create a mobile profile app for performing arts groups where members can list the ensembles they belong to, their role in each one, and any upcoming auditions they are preparing for, with a look that feels artistic and expressive rather than like a spreadsheet. The profile on your phone should feel like it belongs to a real creative community, with a rich layout where your performance history and audition plans both get space to shine.

Need a mobile app where I can browse my message threads and download attachments that people sent me without having to open every single conversation to dig them out, because hunting through old chats for a file someone shared weeks ago is a real pain. On my phone the app should show me a combined list of all the files and photos from my threads so I can tap one and save it straight to my phone.

Need a mobile app with a setting that makes it only sync my data when I am connected to Wi-Fi, so I stop burning through my phone data without knowing it, but I also want a way to manually kick off a sync when I am on mobile data just for that one time. The settings screen on my phone should make the Wi-Fi-only toggle easy to find and the manual sync button should be right there so I do not have to go hunting for it.

Create a mobile app for uploading signed legal contracts where I can either draw my signature right on my phone screen or import a signature image and then attach it to a document before sending it off, because printing and scanning is a huge hassle. The app should walk me through picking the document, adding the signature in the right spot, and confirming the upload all in a few taps so the whole thing takes under a minute.

Build a mobile survey tool where one of the question types lets people answer by taking a photo or picking one from their phone gallery, so respondents can just snap a picture of whatever they are describing instead of typing it all out. The survey flow on my phone should make the photo question feel as easy as the regular text ones, with a clear capture button and a small preview so people know their image was attached before they move on.

Build a mobile thesis submission tool where students can upload several required files at once, like the main document, the cover sheet, and supplementary materials, and see each one go through with a clear status so they know exactly what landed and what still needs to be sent. The app on my phone should handle multiple files in a single submission run and show a confirmation summary so I am not second-guessing whether my work actually went through.

A field inspection photo uploader for my phone where I can take photos on-site and each one automatically gets tagged with my current GPS location before it goes up, so I never have to manually type in where I was standing. The app should show a list of my uploaded photos with a small map pin label on each one, and I can group them by inspection job so everything stays organized without extra effort.

A smart meter data tool on my phone that saves me the hassle of copying numbers by hand, letting me pull my meter readings for any date range and download the whole thing as a CSV file straight to my phone, so I can hand it off to whoever needs it. The app should show the readings in a simple list first so I can check the data looks right before I download.

Make a QA inspection report exporter for the factory floor that works on mobile, where I can fill in the inspection results for each batch right on my phone and then export the whole report as a file I can send to my supervisor. The app should let me pick which production line and date the check was done, then bundle everything into one clean report I can share without having to copy anything manually.

Create a visa document checklist app for my phone that tells me exactly which papers I need to upload for my immigration application and lets me tick off each one as I go. Each item on the list should have an upload spot right next to it so I can attach the file immediately, and the app should show me at a glance which documents are still missing so I stop losing track of what I already submitted.

Make a social media scheduler tool for my phone where I can queue up a bunch of photos and videos at once and set a specific date and time for each batch to go out, so I stop scrambling to post manually every single day. The app should let me pick multiple files in one go, assign them to a scheduled slot, and show me a simple calendar view of everything that is lined up to be posted.

Build a mobile alert rule manager where I can see all my existing alert rules in a list and tap a copy button on any one of them to duplicate it, then just change the number threshold for the new copy without having to fill in every field from scratch. The app should let me give the cloned rule a new name and pick a different metric limit right after copying, so I can set up a whole family of similar alerts without doing the same repetitive work over and over.

Make a config copying tool that works on my phone, where I can see all the settings from my test environment listed out and tap a button to push the whole thing over to the live environment in one shot. The app should show me a side-by-side comparison of what is in each environment before I confirm, so I can catch any differences and avoid accidentally overwriting something important.

Create a tax filing helper app for my phone that pulls in the numbers I entered last year and fills them into this year's form automatically, so I spend less time hunting through old paperwork. The app should show me which fields were copied from last year highlighted, so I can quickly review and update anything that changed, rather than re-typing the same information all over again.

Need a mobile retrospective board tool that lets my team clone a pre-made meeting template at the start of each sprint, so we can skip all the setup and just get straight to filling it in. The app should show a list of saved templates I can copy with one tap, then let everyone add their own notes to the cloned board from their phones during the meeting without overwriting each other.

A customer journey planning tool for my phone where each stage of the journey is its own card, and I can tap any card to make an exact copy of it so I can reuse the same structure for a new stage without typing everything again. The app should let me rename the duplicate and edit just the parts that differ from the original, saving me from rebuilding the same touchpoints and notes from scratch every single time.

Build a loyalty program manager on mobile where I can view all my existing membership tier setups and copy one tier's benefit list to use as a starting point for a new tier, then just tweak the perks and limits instead of writing everything out fresh. The app should let me rename the copied tier and adjust individual benefits one by one, so spinning up a new level takes a minute instead of half a day.

Need a mobile config sync tool that lets me take the current live server settings and copy them down to the test environment with one tap, so I can make sure my tests are running against real conditions. The app should show me a clear summary of what settings are about to be copied before I confirm, and highlight anything that looks different between the two environments so I can decide whether to keep or skip it.

Build a product bundle manager for my phone where I can see all my existing bundles and tap any one to make a copy of it, then update the price and any included items for the new version without starting from zero. The app should let me preview what the copied bundle looks like before saving, so I can quickly roll out a promotional version with adjusted pricing and confirm everything looks right from my phone.

Need a mobile invoice tool that lets me open any past invoice, select the line items I want, and copy them straight into a brand-new invoice so I stop retyping the same services and prices every month. The app should let me pick which items to carry over, adjust the quantities or amounts for the new invoice, and show me a running total as I go so I know the final number before I send it.

Create a shift planner app for my phone where I can set up one week's worth of shift rotations and then duplicate that whole pattern to fill in the next several weeks automatically, instead of manually entering the same schedule over and over. The app should show the repeated weeks in a calendar so I can spot any conflicts and make small edits to specific days without having to redo the whole rotation from scratch.

Need a little mobile app for my phone that shows a paywall screen when a free user tries to use a paid feature, giving them the option to start a free trial before committing to a subscription. The screen should clearly show what they get during the trial period, how long it lasts, and a simple button to start it, so there is no confusion about what they are signing up for.

Create a mobile accessibility checker tool that scans a page and shows me a list of issues it found, grouped by how serious they are, so I can see the biggest problems first. For each issue the app should offer a quick one-tap fix suggestion right there on the phone, so I can clean up the most common problems on the spot without having to dig through documentation to figure out what to do.

Create a biometric setup app for my phone that walks me through enrolling my face and fingerprint one step at a time, so I know exactly what to do and do not get confused by the process. The app should show a clear progress indicator for each enrollment step, let me try the scan again if it does not work the first time, and confirm at the end that both my face and fingerprint are saved and ready to use.

Make a mobile home screen customizer app where I can pick from a list of small info blocks to add to my phone's home screen, and then drag the corners to make each one bigger or smaller so it fits the space I have. The app should show a live preview of how my home screen will look as I add and resize things, so I can arrange everything exactly how I want it before applying the changes.

Need a mobile setup guide app that walks new users through turning on helpful accessibility features on their phone, one feature at a time, so they can find options that make the app easier to use without having to dig through a bunch of settings menus on their own. Each step should show what the feature does in plain language with a simple toggle, and the guide should remember which ones the user already turned on so they can come back and adjust later.

Build a mobile permissions manager app where I can see at a glance which phone apps have access to things like my camera, contacts, and location, all in one place instead of hunting through system settings. The app should let me tap any permission to see which apps have it and turn off access for specific ones right there, so I can clean up all those permissions I said yes to without really thinking about it.

Need a Bluetooth pairing app for my phone that shows nearby devices in a simple list, lets me tap one to connect, and then lets me give each paired device a custom nickname so I can tell them apart. The app should remember all my paired devices and show their nicknames instead of the generic device IDs, so I stop having to guess which one is my speaker and which one is my headphones every single time.

A calendar sync setup tool for my phone that lets me connect my Google or work calendar account and choose which of those calendars I want to show up in my main calendar app, so all my events land in one place. The app should walk me through linking each account step by step and let me toggle individual calendars on or off after connecting, so I have full control over what shows up on my phone.

Build a data import helper app for my phone that lets me bring in a file from another app or service and then match up the columns from that file to the right fields in my app, so the data lands in the correct place. The app should show me a side-by-side preview of how the imported data will look after matching, and let me correct any mismatches before confirming, so I stop ending up with names in the wrong column or dates in the wrong format.

Create a mobile link router app that intercepts shared links on my phone and, when a link could open in more than one app, shows me a quick picker listing all the options so I can choose where it goes each time. The app should remember my preferred choices for common link types and let me update those defaults from a simple settings list, so I stop being sent to the wrong app by accident.
